candidates.detail: ArchitecturalPlanPoint admits any finite f32 pair. PlanPolygon::from_ordered_vertices promises finite nondegenerate counterclockwise convex vertices, but its signed_area subtracts the first point after widening each f32 coordinate to f64 and treats an exactly zero computed sum as degenerate. Widening avoids f32 range overflow but cannot preserve every difference between f32 coordinates at vastly different exponents.
candidates.source_only_case: Let M=2^60, exactly representable and finite in f32, and use ordered points A=(M,M), B=(0,0), C=(1,0). All three points are distinct and finite; their exact determinant (B−A)×(C−A) is M > 0, so the triangle is counterclockwise with area M/2. At f64 precision, the nearest representable value below M is M−128, so 1−M rounds to −M. The translated vectors for B and C both become (−M,−M); their computed determinant and signed_area are zero, and the constructor returns DegeneratePolygon before its duplicate or convexity checks. This is integer/IEEE reasoning from source, not an executed constructor, product test or runtime probe.
candidates.consumer_and_safeguards: ScenePlanPolygon::from_ordered_vertices delegates to the same PlanPolygon constructor for finite scene points; FloorRegion wire admission reconstructs either a scene polygon or an architectural polygon before projection, so the same rejection can propagate if an input of that shape reaches those paths. Ground-contact and floor-footprint source uses the related PlanHull cross predicate, but this particular witness has not been shown to misclassify a hull. ScenePlanPolygon::from_architectural deliberately uses its own rounding-aware rigid-projection policy; this observation does not propose replacing that path with strict arbitrary-polygon revalidation. No ordinary generated city, real transport input, terrain or gameplay failure is demonstrated.
